items.t: Collingwood, Vancouver: 40 houses sold at a median of $1,510,000, with the middle half between $1,349,185 and $1,742,500. The median house took 20 days to sell and closed at 96.2% of list.

26 townhomes sold in Collingwood, Vancouver at a median of $981,500 (middle half $844,000 to $1,053,750). A typical townhome in Collingwood, Vancouver spent 16 days on the market and closed at 98.5% of the asking price.
In Collingwood, Vancouver, condos sold at a median of $520,000 across 149 sales, and the middle half closed between $470,000 and $648,776. The median condo sat 22 days and sold for 97.3% of list.
Collingwood, Vancouver: 36 duplexes sold at a median of $1,315,000, with the middle half between $1,072,500 and $1,491,625. The median duplex took 37 days to sell and closed at 95.2% of list.

How Collingwood compares with the rest of Vancouver East

items.t: Houses in Collingwood have the lowest median of the 15 Vancouver East sub-areas, $1,510,000, below Victoria VE at $1,528,000; the highest is Fraser at $1,980,000.

Of 13 Vancouver East sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Collingwood ranks 9th highest at $981,500; the range is $796,000 (Killarney) to $1,419,500 (Main). South Marine ($943,750) sits just below and Renfrew VE ($1,044,400) sits just above.
Condos in Collingwood have the lowest median of the 13 Vancouver East sub-areas, $520,000, below Victoria VE at $533,000; the highest is Main at $898,950.

Of 15 Vancouver East sub-areas with 5 or more duplex sales, Collingwood ranks 12th highest at $1,315,000; the range is $1,112,500 (Strathcona) to $1,919,000 (Main). Fraserview VE ($1,243,250) sits just below and South Vancouver ($1,331,500) sits just above.
